derivations.claim: The equations, coefficients, state functions, and spatial derivatives in [A1] match the hypotheses and definitions of [F1]. Applying its exact identities gives $\partial_t s_{\mathrm{eff}}+\operatorname{div}j_s=|q|^2/(\kappa T_0^2)$ and $\partial_t e_L+\operatorname{div}(\vartheta q)=-|q|^2/\kappa$. Since $\kappa,T_0,C,\tau$ are positive, the production is nonnegative and $e_L$ is positive definite in $(\vartheta,q)$. These are deductions for the adopted effective current and linear subsystem.

Differentiate the first equation of [A1] in time and take the divergence of its second equation. Substituting $\operatorname{div}q=-C\vartheta_t$ and $\operatorname{div}q_t=-C\vartheta_{tt}$ gives $\tau\vartheta_{tt}+\vartheta_t-(\kappa/C)\Delta\vartheta=0$. By [F2] its characteristic speed is $v_h=\sqrt{\kappa/(C\tau)}$. All coefficients and $c$ are positive, so squaring the nonnegative quantities preserves order: $v_h\leq c$ is equivalent to $\kappa/(C\tau)\leq c^2$, and multiplication by $C\tau>0$ gives $\kappa\leq C\tau c^2$. Reversing these steps proves the converse.

For the stated Schwartz or smooth-periodic initial data, [F3] supplies the unique global smooth evolution, weighted-norm contraction, and finite propagation at $v_h$, conditional on its exact generic linear-supplier hypotheses and $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ assumption [F5]. In the periodic case [F3] also gives $|\vartheta(t,x)|\leq K_{r,L,C}\|U(t)\|_{H^r_M}\leq K_{r,L,C}\|U_0\|_{H^r_M}$ for the stated $r$; if the last quantity is less than $T_0$, then $T_0+\vartheta(t,x)>0$. The data class is the componentwise class defined in [F4]. This proves the stated positivity qualification without claiming that the solution remains in $D$.

derivations.claim: The assumed strict inequality gives $\Omega>0$. Write $\phi(t)=e^{-t/(2\tau)}y(t)$ with $y(t)=A\cos(\Omega t)$. Differentiation yields $\phi''+\tau^{-1}\phi'+(\kappa k^2/(C\tau))\phi=e^{-t/(2\tau)}[y''+\Omega^2 y]=0$, because $y''=-\Omega^2y$ and $\Omega^2=\kappa k^2/(C\tau)-1/(4\tau^2)$. Thus $\phi$ solves the one-mode telegrapher equation from [F2].

Differentiating the displayed temperature field in time gives $C\vartheta_t=C\phi'(t)\cos(kx_1)$, while differentiating the first component of $q$ in space gives $\operatorname{div}q=-C\phi'(t)\cos(kx_1)$. Their sum is zero, so the thermal-energy balance in [F1] holds pointwise.

The flux satisfies $\tau q_t+q=-(C/k)(\tau\phi''+\phi')\sin(kx_1)e_1$. The mode equation in step 1.1 is equivalent to $-(C/k)(\tau\phi''+\phi')=\kappa k\phi$. Since $\nabla\vartheta=-k\phi\sin(kx_1)e_1$, this equals $-\kappa\nabla\vartheta$, proving the Cattaneo relation in [F1] pointwise.

For $t\geq0$, $|\vartheta(t,x)|\leq |A|e^{-t/(2\tau)}\leq|A|$, and $|\phi'(t)|\leq |A|e^{-t/(2\tau)}(1/(2\tau)+\Omega)$, so $|q(t,x)|\leq(C/k)|A|(1/(2\tau)+\Omega)$. Because $D$ in [F3] is open and contains $(0,0)$, choose $\delta_T,\delta_q>0$ with $(-\delta_T,\delta_T)\times\{q:|q|<\delta_q\}\subseteq D$; then any nonzero $A$ satisfying $|A|<\min(T_0,\delta_T)$ and $(C/k)|A|(1/(2\tau)+\Omega)<\delta_q$ keeps the entire forward solution in $D$ and gives $T_0+\vartheta\geq T_0-|A|>0$.
